title: I/O at the edges
summary: Read and write through TextReader and TextWriter so tests can feed input and capture output.

steps.title: Console is a hidden dependency too
body: `Console.ReadLine` is a hidden input and `Console.WriteLine` a hidden output. .NET gives you the seam for free: `Console.In` is a `TextReader`, `Console.Out` is a `TextWriter`. Accept those types instead:
Run(new StringReader("Ada"), sw);                   // test: sw.ToString() is "Hello, Ada\n"

steps.prompt: Your code reads `prices.csv` with `File.ReadAllLines(path)`. What is the most testable shape?
options: Parse from a `TextReader` (or a list of lines); only the outer shell opens the file
Keep the file read but use a test file on the C: drive
Read the path from an environment variable

steps.title: Keep I/O thin
body: The goal is not just to swap `Console` for `TextWriter`. It is to push I/O to the **edges** so the logic in the middle does not do I/O at all:
var report = BuildReport(lines);       // core: pure, easy to test
`BuildReport` takes data and returns data. You test it with plain lists and strings, no readers or files needed. Readers and writers are for the thin layer that remains.

items: Opening a file and reading its lines
Writing the report to the console
Parsing a CSV line into a record

steps.prompt: Capture what a method writes in a test.

steps.title: Take readers and writers
prompt: `Tally` reads numbers from the console until a blank line and prints the total. Make it testable:
`void Tally(TextReader input, TextWriter output)` reads lines until `null` or an empty line, and writes `Total: <sum>`.
template: string DojoRun(string text) { var w = new StringWriter(); Tally(new StringReader(text), w); return w.ToString().Trim(); }
Dojo.Eq("stops at a blank line", "Total: 5", DojoRun("5\n\n100"));

steps.title: Split edge from core
prompt: Pull the logic out of the I/O:
- `string Report(IEnumerable<string> lines)`: each line is `name,score`; return `<best name> wins with <score>` (first wins ties). **No** I/O.
- `void Main(TextReader input, TextWriter output)` reads all lines from `input` (until `null`), calls `Report`, writes the result.
starter: if (score > bestScore) { best = parts[0]; bestScore = score; }
template: Dojo.Eq("first wins a tie", "Al wins with 5", Report(new List<string> { "Al,5", "Bo,5" }));
hints: Collect lines into a `List<string>` in `Main`, then call `Report`.
In `Report`, keep a running best with a loop or `Aggregate`; only replace it when the score is strictly greater.
